savings.caption:
Wind and solar have kept Britain from needing gas imports worth £5.9bn since the Hormuz crisis began in February 2026, according to Carbon Brief. Bringing that gas in would have taken more than 100 extra tanker deliveries of liquefied gas.

In 2026 up to late September, wind and solar made a record 41% of the UK's electricity, and gas made 25%. The more wind and solar make, the less gas needs burning for power, and this year gas has been expensive.

The £5.9bn is the value of the gas imports avoided at this year's prices, as worked out by Carbon Brief.
